scenes.say: Ever wonder why Maven splits builds into phases? What do those steps actually control?
Maven's lifecycle is a series of phases. It starts by checking your project, then compiles, tests, packages, and finally installs your build locally.

scenes.label: Plugins
scenes.sub: Plugins attach custom actions to any phase
scenes.say: You can hook plugins to any phase, so extra steps like code analysis or deployment fit right into the flow.

scenes.title: Run up to 'test' phase
scenes.say: For example, running the test command compiles your code and runs all your unit tests automatically.

scenes.question: Does 'mvn test' only run tests?
scenes.wrong: Yes, it skips compile and package.
scenes.right: No, it compiles first, then runs tests.
scenes.say: Here's a classic interview trap: does running the test command only run tests? Not quite. Maven always completes earlier phases first, so it compiles before testing.
